name: Cartan exterior differential calculus
summary: Cartan developed the exterior derivative and used it with Pfaffian systems and moving frames to unify differential geometry with Lie theory.

name: Axiomatisation of geometry
summary: Hilbert gave a complete independent axiom system for Euclidean geometry that did not rely on diagrams, and used models to test independence.

name: Descriptive set theory
summary: Baire, Lebesgue, Suslin and Lusin explored regularity of definable sets, leading to analytic and projective sets.

name: Brownian motion: from physics and finance to measure on path space
summary: A random motion modelled by physicists and by Bachelier is given a rigorous measure on continuous paths, which then solves boundary value problems for harmonic functions.

name: Calculus of variations to Hilbert's direct methods
summary: Hilbert justified Dirichlet's principle with direct variational methods, rescuing Riemann's use of minimisation in complex analysis.

name: Fredholm integral equations
summary: Fredholm treated integral equations as limits of linear algebraic systems and solved the Dirichlet problem.

name: Russell paradox, type theory and Principia Mathematica
summary: Russell's paradox led to the ramified theory of types and the formal derivation of mathematics.

name: Schur: polynomial representations of GL(n) and invariant theory
summary: Schur's thesis used Frobenius methods to classify rational representations of the general linear group, tying them to symmetric functions.

name: Hilbert space and integral equations
from: quadratic forms in infinitely many variables
summary: Hilbert and Riesz made sequence and function spaces into an infinite-dimensional geometry with spectral theory.

name: Axiomatic set theory (Zermelo)
summary: Zermelo proved well-ordering from choice and axiomatized set theory.
